claims.title: The proto-urban settlement of Sarazm
claims.summary: In the Zeravshan valley near Penjikent, Sarazm grows into one of the oldest proto-urban settlements in Central Asia, a centre of metallurgy and long-distance trade, later inscribed as Tajikistan's first UNESCO World Heritage Site (2010).

claims.title: Alexander the Great in Sogdiana and Bactria
claims.summary: After overthrowing the Achaemenid Persians, Alexander the Great campaigns through Sogdiana and Bactria, the Iranian lands of Transoxania that later peoples would regard as the Tajik homeland.

sources.label: Sogdiana — Central Asia, Silk Road, Persian Empire

claims.title: Sogdian merchants dominate the Silk Road
claims.summary: Sogdian traders from Samarkand and Penjikent become the principal caravan merchants of the Silk Road, and the Sogdian language serves as the commercial lingua franca of Central Asia.

sources.label: Sogdiana — Central Asia, Silk Road, Persian Empire

claims.title: The Samanid Empire centred on Bukhara
claims.summary: The Persian Samanid dynasty rules eastern Iran and Central Asia from Bukhara, making the city a focal point of Islamic civilisation and a hub of Persianate culture.

sources.label: Sogdiana — Central Asia, Silk Road, Persian Empire

claims.title: The reign of Ismail Samani
claims.summary: Ismail I ibn Ahmad unifies the Samanid realm and rules from Bukhara as one of the dynasty's most famous sovereigns; he is revered today as a founding symbol of the Tajik nation.

sources.label: Kazakstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan: Country Studies

claims.title: Rudaki and the rebirth of Persian poetry
claims.summary: At the Samanid court in Bukhara, the poet Rudaki composes in New Persian and is honoured as the father of Persian poetry, anchoring the literary heritage Tajiks claim as their own.

claims.title: Karakhanid conquest of Bukhara
claims.summary: The Turkic Karakhanids capture Bukhara, ending Samanid rule in Transoxania and opening centuries of Turkic and Mongol domination over the region.

claims.title: The Mongol conquest of Transoxania
claims.summary: Genghis Khan's armies sweep through Central Asia, sacking Bukhara and Samarkand, ushering in centuries of Mongol and Turko-Mongol rule over the Persian-speaking population.

claims.title: Timur makes Samarkand his capital
claims.summary: The conqueror Timur (Tamerlane) builds a Timurid empire centred on Samarkand, whose courts become renowned centres of Persianate art, science and architecture.

claims.title: Division between Bukhara and Kokand
claims.summary: The territory of present-day Tajikistan is split mainly between the Emirate of Bukhara, which holds the south, and the Khanate of Kokand, which controls the northern Ferghana fringe.

claims.title: Bukhara becomes a Russian protectorate
claims.summary: Defeated by Russian forces, the Emir of Bukhara accepts Russian terms in 1868; the emirate becomes a protectorate and the northern Tajik lands are absorbed into Russian Turkestan.

claims.title: Creation of the Tajik ASSR
claims.summary: In the Soviet national delimitation of Central Asia, a Tajik Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic is established within the Uzbek SSR, with Dushanbe as its capital.

claims.title: The Tajik SSR and the loss of Bukhara and Samarkand
claims.summary: The Tajik ASSR is detached from Uzbekistan and elevated to a full union republic, but the historic Persian-speaking cities of Bukhara and Samarkand are left within the Uzbek SSR.

claims.title: Declaration of independence
claims.summary: As the Soviet Union disintegrates, the Supreme Soviet of the Tajik SSR declares the state independence of the Republic of Tajikistan — the country's founding moment and national day.

claims.title: The Tajik civil war
claims.summary: Civil war erupts between the post-communist government and an Islamic-democratic opposition alliance; it causes massive displacement and a death toll that remains contested and is best treated as an estimate.

claims.title: Emomali Rahmon elected president; UNMOT established
claims.summary: Emomali Rahmon, leader of the government side since 1992, is elected president; the UN establishes the Mission of Observers in Tajikistan (UNMOT) to monitor the ceasefire.

claims.title: UN-brokered General Peace Agreement
claims.summary: President Rahmon and United Tajik Opposition leader Said Abdullo Nuri sign the General Agreement on the Establishment of Peace and National Accord in Moscow, ending the civil war under UN auspices.

claims.title: Tajik National Park inscribed by UNESCO
claims.summary: The Tajik National Park (Mountains of the Pamirs), covering roughly 18 per cent of the country, becomes Tajikistan's first natural World Heritage Site, protecting the 'Roof of the World'.

claims.title: A remittance-dependent economy
claims.summary: Remittances from Tajik labour migrants, mostly working in Russia, reach close to half of GDP — among the highest shares in the world — leaving the economy heavily exposed to external shocks.
